Report: whisper hallucination options, cheapest/already-effort first. (1) VAD gating with Silero -- ALREADY ON: Servex/Servex.js:498-505 runs whisper-server.exe (ggml-large-v3-turbo.bin) with --vad --vad-model ggml-silero-v5.1.2.bin, cited as the biggest win against silence hallucinations (github.com/ggml-org/whisper.cpp/issues/1026). Risk: can clip start of real quiet speech if padding too short (no padding flag set). (2) no_speech_thold/logprob_thold -- whisper.cpp exposes these but a 2026 report says v1.9.2 returns 0.000 for every segment's no_speech_prob, making the threshold inert (github.com/raullenchai/Rapid-MLX/issues/960); verify before relying on it. (3) -mc 0 (condition_on_previous_text off) -- stops one hallucinated window seeding a repeat loop in the next (same issue #1026); 1-line flag add to Servex.js args; no real risk. (4) --suppress-nst (suppress non-speech tokens) -- built into whisper.cpp; 1-line flag add; small risk of dropping legit filler tokens. (5) client-side energy/level gate before calling whisper-server -- a few lines in ux/Dictate's capture code (not located this pass); risk of clipping quiet speech if floor set too high. (6) hallucination phrase blocklist (drop exact 'Thank you.'/'Thanks for watching'/'you' ONLY when no_speech_prob is high or energy near zero, never on text alone) -- cheap backstop, small file change in WhisperLogRows.js area (dograh.com/feeds/blog/whisper-hallucination-silence, yaps.ai/blog/whisper-hallucination). (7) model swap large-v3 vs large-v3-turbo -- turbo (4 decoder layers vs 32, 809M vs 1.54B params) is ~4x faster, ~1-2% WER increase same-language, degrades more on some languages (huggingface.co/openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo); no turbo-specific hallucination-rate data found, not worth switching for this alone. Recommend trying first: -mc 0 and --suppress-nst, both one-line additions to the existing whisper-server args in Servex.js, zero new risk.
